items.author: Danny Green
paragraphs: Adlai Nortye, Omada Health, Syndax, Six Flags, and Immunic Lead Market Declines
Several stocks recorded double-digit losses on October 13, 2026.
A failed clinical trial drove the decline in Syndax Pharmaceuticals.
Six Flags shares fell following a fatal roller-coaster incident, while no clear catalysts were identified for the other declines.
On October 13, 2026, Adlai Nortye (NASDAQ: ANL) fell 17.3% to $11.76 on about 958,000 shares. No company-specific news clearly explained the decline.

Omada Health (NASDAQ: OMDA) dropped 16.3% to $18.30, with approximately 2.8 million shares traded. The company plans to report third-quarter results after the market closes on November 5, 2026, but the announcement did not explain the selloff.

Syndax Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ: SNDX) declined 15.7% to $13.95. Its Phase 2 MAXPIRe trial of axatilimab in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis failed to meet its primary endpoint, prompting the company to end development of the drug for that indication.

Six Flags Entertainment (NYSE: FUN) fell 14.4% to $10.20 after a fatal roller-coaster incident at Six Flags Over Georgia. The company temporarily closed nine similar coasters across six North American parks.
Immunic (NASDAQ: IMUX) declined 13.3% to $6.89 on approximately 572,000 shares. No new company announcement was identified as a clear cause of the drop.

items.title: Bumble (NASDAQ: BMBL) Leads Sharp Stock-Market Gains
items.excerpt: Bumble (NASDAQ: BMBL) surged 56.6% after agreeing to be acquired by Ithaca Holdings. Enerflex (NYSE: EFXT) gained 14.4% following a major data-center power contract. Picard Medical, Julong Holding, and Regencell Bioscience also advanced sharply, although no clear same-day catalys
items.author: Gordon Thompson
paragraphs: Bumble (NASDAQ: BMBL) surged 56.6% after agreeing to be acquired by Ithaca Holdings.
Enerflex (NYSE: EFXT) gained 14.4% following a major data-center power contract.
Picard Medical, Julong Holding, and Regencell Bioscience also advanced sharply, although no clear same-day catalysts were identified.

On October 13, 2026, Bumble (NASDAQ: BMBL) jumped 56.6% to $5.95 after Ithaca Holdings agreed to acquire the company for $6.05 per share in cash, valuing the transaction at approximately $1.3 billion. Trading volume reached about 118 million shares.
Picard Medical (NYSE American: PMI) rose 35.2% to $15.33. No new company announcement clearly explained the rally.

Julong Holding (NASDAQ: JLHL) climbed 16.8% to $5.15. The company previously announced a private placement expected to generate $897,750 in gross proceeds, but no direct connection to the day’s gain was established.
Regencell Bioscience (NASDAQ: RGC) advanced 14.9% to $8.19, with volume nearly three times its average. No clear same-day catalyst was identified.

Enerflex (NYSE: EFXT) gained 14.4% to $27.54 after securing a contract to supply more than one gigawatt of natural-gas-fired power-generation equipment for a North American data-center project. Its U.S. ticker is EFXT; EFX is its Toronto Stock Exchange ticker.

items.title: Applied Materials (NASDAQ: AMAT) Outlook: AI-Driven Growth and Financial Targets
items.excerpt: Cantor Fitzgerald maintains an Outperform rating on Applied Materials despite a recent stock dip. The company anticipates sustained demand for its chipmaking equipment, fueled by AI infrastructure buildout. Applied Materials projects significant market share gains and strong fina
items.author: Gordon Thompson
paragraphs: Cantor Fitzgerald maintains an Outperform rating on Applied Materials despite a recent stock dip.
The company anticipates sustained demand for its chipmaking equipment, fueled by AI infrastructure buildout.
Applied Materials projects significant market share gains and strong financial performance (gross margin, operating margin, free cash flow return) by 2030.

Applied Materials (NASDAQ: AMAT) makes equipment used to produce computer chips. Cantor Fitzgerald maintains its Outperform rating, with the action listed as hold. The stock trades at $464.17 when the update is posted.

The shares are down $33.36, or 6.71%, at that price. They trade between $452.81 and $485.40 during the day. As highlighted by 24/7 Wall Street, investors take profits in chip-equipment stocks after a strong year driven by artificial intelligence spending. Competitors Lam Research (NASDAQ: LRCX) and KLA (NASDAQ: KLAC) each fall about 4%.

At its October 13 SEMICON West investor presentation, Applied Materials says the buildout of AI infrastructure supports demand for its equipment over several years. It points to tools used in advanced chipmaking, memory production and packaging, which connects separate chip components.

Applied Materials expects spending on wafer fab equipment—the machines used to make chips—to grow faster through 2030 than it does over the past decade. The company aims to gain more than 2 percentage points of that market from 2025 to 2030.

By 2030, Applied Materials targets a non-GAAP gross margin of about 54% and a non-GAAP operating margin of about 40%. Those measures show how much revenue remains after certain costs, with non-GAAP figures excluding some accounting items. Applied Materials also plans to return 80% to 100% of free cash flow, the cash left after capital spending, to shareholders over time.

items.title: Ollie's Bargain Outlet (NASDAQ: OLLI) Stock: Price Target and Share Buyback Boost Investor Confidence
items.excerpt: Gordon Haskett Capital Corporation set a $105 price target for Ollie's Bargain Outlet , indicating an 18.1% upside from its trading price. The company's board approved an additional $500 million share repurchase authorization, bringing the total available for buybacks to $561 mil
items.author: Andrew Wynn
paragraphs: Gordon Haskett Capital Corporation set a $105 price target for Ollie's Bargain Outlet, indicating an 18.1% upside from its trading price.
The company's board approved an additional $500 million share repurchase authorization, bringing the total available for buybacks to $561 million.
CEO Eric van der Valk highlighted the share repurchase as a sign of confidence in Ollie's long-term growth, cash generation, and financial position.

Ollie’s Bargain Outlet (NASDAQ: OLLI) sells discounted brand-name goods through its stores. On October 13, 2026, Gordon Haskett Capital Corporation set a $105 price target for the stock. With shares trading at about $88.90 at the time, that target represents approximately 18.1% upside, signaling a potential investment opportunity for investors.

The target comes as Ollie’s expands its ability to buy back shares. Its board unanimously approves an additional $500 million share repurchase authorization, bringing the total available for buybacks to approximately $561 million, as highlighted by GlobeNewswire. This significant share repurchase program underscores the company's financial strength.

A repurchase allows a company to buy its own shares. It can reduce the number of shares available to investors, though the authorization does not mean Ollie’s must spend the full amount. CEO Eric van der Valk says the decision reflects confidence in the company’s long-term growth, cash generation, and robust financial position, which are key indicators for stock analysis.

Ollie’s Bargain Outlet trades at $89.03, up $2.59, or 3.00%. Shares have traded between $87.95 and $93.88 today, compared with a range of $60.29 to $133.28 over the past year. The company’s market value is approximately $5.38 billion, and trading volume is 1.26 million shares, reflecting active stock performance.

items.title: H.C. Wainwright Adjusts Price Target for AngioDynamics (NASDAQ: ANGO) Amid Q1 Fiscal 2027 Results
items.excerpt: H.C. Wainwright maintained its Buy rating on AngioDynamics but lowered its price target to $18 . AngioDynamics reported a 6.9% revenue increase to $80.9 million and a narrowed adjusted loss of 4 cents per share for Q1 fiscal 2027. Despite positive Q1 results and strong Med Tech s
items.author: Andrew Wynn
paragraphs: H.C. Wainwright maintained its Buy rating on AngioDynamics but lowered its price target to $18.
AngioDynamics reported a 6.9% revenue increase to $80.9 million and a narrowed adjusted loss of 4 cents per share for Q1 fiscal 2027.
Despite positive Q1 results and strong Med Tech sales, AngioDynamics' shares experienced a significant drop of over 21%.

H.C. Wainwright maintains its Buy rating on AngioDynamics (NASDAQ: ANGO) but lowers its price target from $19 to $18. The medical device stock trades at $10.68 when the update is posted. AngioDynamics makes medical devices, including its Auryon, AlphaVac and NanoKnife products.

The rating update follows AngioDynamics’ first-quarter fiscal 2027 results. Revenue rises 6.9% from a year earlier to $80.9 million. The adjusted loss narrows to 4 cents per share from 10 cents a year earlier. An adjusted loss excludes certain costs, giving investors another way to track the company’s operating performance and financial health.

Med Tech sales grow 13.2% to $39.9 million, with AlphaVac sales up 37.4%. Gross margin reaches 59.4%, an increase of 410 basis points, or 4.1 percentage points. Gross margin shows how much sales revenue remains after direct production costs. The operating loss narrows to $7.3 million, as highlighted by Zacks.

The stronger Q1 fiscal results do not prevent a sharp share-price drop. Shares fall more than 21% on Thursday despite beating analysts’ earnings expectations, as highlighted by Benzinga. About 1.94 million shares change hands, nearly 3.8 times the 100-day average. AngioDynamics also names Eric Honroth president and CEO, effective Nov. 2, succeeding Jim Clemmer.

items.title: Domino's Pizza (NASDAQ:DPZ) Q3 Earnings: Navigating Competition and Stock Performance
items.excerpt: Domino's Pizza (NASDAQ:DPZ) reported strong Q3 2026 earnings per share of $4.60 , surpassing analyst estimates, despite slower revenue growth of 3.4% . Domino's same-store sales growth remained modest at 0.3% in the U.S. and 0.2% internationally, indicating competitive market con
items.author: Andrew Wynn
paragraphs: Domino's Pizza (NASDAQ:DPZ) reported strong Q3 2026 earnings per share of $4.60, surpassing analyst estimates, despite slower revenue growth of 3.4%.
Domino's same-store sales growth remained modest at 0.3% in the U.S. and 0.2% internationally, indicating competitive market conditions and cautious consumer spending.
Year-to-date free cash flow saw a 7.2% decline to $459.8 million, with the stock trading around $301.35 following the report.

Domino’s Pizza (NASDAQ:DPZ) operates a global pizza delivery and carryout business. It competes with other pizza chains and local restaurants. Cowen & Co. maintains a Hold investment rating on Domino’s, meaning it does not recommend buying or selling the DPZ stock at this time. Shares trade at $301.40 when the rating is posted.

Domino’s reports third-quarter 2026 earnings of $4.60 per share, up 12.7% and above analysts’ $4.37 estimate. Revenue rises 3.4% to $1.19 billion, while net income increases 9.2% to $152.2 million. Seeking Alpha publishes a transcript of the earnings call, though the provided news item includes no financial results or executive comments.

Sales growth is much slower than earnings growth. U.S. same-store sales, which measure sales at existing locations, rise 0.3%. International same-store sales increase 0.2% after excluding currency effects. Domino’s adds a net 175 stores worldwide, but expects muted annual same-store sales as competition and cautious consumers weigh on demand, as highlighted by Reuters.

Year-to-date free cash flow falls 7.2% to $459.8 million. Free cash flow is the cash left after a company pays for its operations and investments. The results are Domino’s first quarterly report under CEO Joe Jordan. Domino’s also trades at $301.35, down $9.55, or 3.07%, near the $301.40 price cited with Cowen’s rating.

items.title: Citigroup (NYSE: C) Exceeds Q3 2026 Earnings Estimates with Strong Trading Performance
items.excerpt: Citigroup (NYSE: C) reported robust Q3 2026 earnings, surpassing analyst estimates for both EPS and revenue. Exceptional performance in fixed-income trading and services significantly contributed to the positive financial results. The bank's profit surged 40% , driven by growth i
items.author: Gordon Thompson
paragraphs: Citigroup (NYSE: C) reported robust Q3 2026 earnings, surpassing analyst estimates for both EPS and revenue.
Exceptional performance in fixed-income trading and services significantly contributed to the positive financial results.
The bank's profit surged 40%, driven by growth in investment banking, services, and wealth management.

Citigroup (NYSE: C), a leading global bank, operates diverse businesses including trading, investment banking, wealth management, and financial services. The company announced its third-quarter 2026 earnings before the market opened on October 13. Earnings per share reached $2.85, significantly exceeding the $2.65 estimate. Furthermore, revenue stood at $23.8 billion, compared with the $23.7 billion estimate, showcasing robust financial performance.

Citigroup’s fixed-income traders delivered their strongest third quarter in at least a decade, a key highlight for the global financial institution. Performance in fixed-income, currency, and commodities trading, alongside its services division, surpassed analyst expectations. These strong results helped to mitigate a slower quarter for Citi’s mergers-and-acquisitions advisory business, which generates fees from advising companies on strategic deals.

Overall profit for the bank rose 40%, as highlighted by Reuters, demonstrating significant growth in the financial sector. This increase was primarily driven by higher revenue from investment banking, services, and wealth management. The exceptional trading results further contributed to lifting quarterly revenue to one of the bank’s highest levels ever, underscoring Citigroup's strong market position.

Citi’s trailing price-to-earnings ratio stands at 13.45, indicating that its share price is 13.45 times its earnings over the past year. Its price-to-sales ratio is 1.25, meaning there is $1.25 in market value for each $1 of annual revenue. These key financial measures provide investors with crucial context for evaluating the reported earnings and revenue performance of the bank.

items.title: State Street (NYSE: STT) Q3 2026 Earnings Preview: What Investors Should Watch
items.excerpt: Differing Q3 2026 earnings and revenue forecasts from Wall Street and Zacks. Strong projected growth in earnings ( 31.3% ), revenue ( 14% ), net interest income ( 19.8% ), and service fees ( 12.9% ). Potential headwinds from higher operating expenses and technology/expansion cost
items.author: Gordon Thompson
paragraphs: Differing Q3 2026 earnings and revenue forecasts from Wall Street and Zacks.
Strong projected growth in earnings (31.3%), revenue (14%), net interest income (19.8%), and service fees (12.9%).
Potential headwinds from higher operating expenses and technology/expansion costs, despite record assets under management.

State Street (NYSE: STT) is scheduled to report its third-quarter 2026 earnings before the market opens on Wednesday, October 14. As a leading provider of investment services and asset management for institutional clients, State Street's results are closely watched. On the same day, investors will also be able to compare its performance with other major financial firms reporting, including Morgan Stanley (NYSE: MS) and BlackRock (NYSE: BLK).

Wall Street estimates for State Street's Q3 earnings are set at $3.68 per share, with revenue projected to be approximately $4.03 billion. A separate Zacks preview offers a slightly different financial outlook, forecasting earnings of $3.63 per share and revenue of $4.04 billion. It's important to note that these figures represent analyst forecasts and not actual reported results.

As highlighted by Zacks, earnings are expected to see significant growth, rising 31.3% from a year earlier, while revenue is anticipated to grow by 14%. Zacks further projects a 19.8% growth in net interest income, which represents income earned on assets after interest costs, and a 12.9% growth in revenue from service fees. These projections underscore the expected strong financial performance.

State Street successfully beat the Zacks earnings estimate in the second quarter, driven by robust growth in fee revenue and net interest income. Furthermore, assets held or managed for clients reached record levels. However, higher operating expenses remained a drag, and ongoing technology and expansion costs could potentially weigh on the upcoming Q3 results. Reflecting broader investor sentiment, Jim Cramer commented that the three financial firms reporting on Wednesday are “priced for disappointment,” suggesting that market expectations for their financial results might be subdued.

items.title: BioNTech BNT113 Misses First Trial Endpoint
items.excerpt: BioNTech (NASDAQ: BNTX) Clinical Trial Update: BNT113 Misses First Primary Endpoint BioNTech’s investigational mRNA cancer immunotherapy BNT113, combined with pembrolizumab, did not produce a statistically significant improvement in progression-free survival. The AHEAD-MERI
items.author: Tony Dante
paragraphs: BioNTech (NASDAQ: BNTX) Clinical Trial Update: BNT113 Misses First Primary Endpoint
BioNTech’s investigational mRNA cancer immunotherapy BNT113, combined with pembrolizumab, did not produce a statistically significant improvement in progression-free survival.
The AHEAD-MERIT Phase 2/3 trial will continue to evaluate overall survival, its second primary endpoint.
BioNTech shares declined following the update, while Citi maintained its Buy rating and $125 price target.

BioNTech (NASDAQ: BNTX) develops immunotherapies, including mRNA-based cancer treatments. Citi maintained its Buy rating and $125 price target after the BNT113 trial update, indicating that the firm still sees a potential development path for the treatment.

BioNTech announced that BNT113, combined with pembrolizumab, did not produce a statistically significant improvement in progression-free survival compared with pembrolizumab alone. The result came from the randomized portion of the AHEAD-MERIT Phase 2/3 trial involving patients with unresectable recurrent or metastatic HPV16-positive, PD-L1-positive head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.

Progression-free survival is the length of time patients live without their cancer worsening. It is the first of the trial’s two primary endpoints. The Independent Data Monitoring Committee recommended that the study continue as planned to evaluate overall survival. Under the trial’s predefined statistical design, a statistically significant overall-survival improvement could still establish a positive trial outcome despite the missed progression-free survival endpoint. BioNTech remains blinded to the continuing trial data.

Moderna (NASDAQ: MRNA) has experienced much stronger stock performance in 2026. According to The Motley Fool, Moderna shares had gained more than 660% year to date by October 13, while BioNTech was only slightly positive. Moderna’s market capitalization was close to $90 billion, approximately 3.6 times BioNTech’s valuation of less than $25 billion. The difference reflects their recent clinical results and investor expectations, although market capitalization alone does not determine which company has the stronger long-term pipeline.

Moderna and Merck (NYSE: MRK) reported positive Phase 3 results for intismeran autogene, an individualized mRNA-based cancer therapy, combined with Keytruda in patients with surgically removed high-risk melanoma. The trial met its primary recurrence-free-survival endpoint and a key secondary endpoint measuring distant metastasis-free survival. Overall-survival follow-up is continuing.

BioNTech shares traded near $90.60 around midday on October 13, down approximately 5.5% following the clinical update. The stock’s intraday range was $89.78–$93.08, its 52-week range was $79.52–$124.00, and its market capitalization was approximately $22.8 billion. These figures were recorded while the market was still open and could change before the closing bell.

items.excerpt: Wells Fargo (NYSE:WFC) reported Q3 2026 EPS of $1.87 , surpassing analyst estimates of $1.85 . Despite the EPS beat , revenue of $21.87 billion fell short of the $22.31 billion estimate. Wealth and Investment Management revenue grew 12% to $4.1 billion , and return on equity reac
items.author: Andrew Wynn
paragraphs: Wells Fargo (NYSE:WFC) reported Q3 2026 EPS of $1.87, surpassing analyst estimates of $1.85.
Despite the EPS beat, revenue of $21.87 billion fell short of the $22.31 billion estimate.
Wealth and Investment Management revenue grew 12% to $4.1 billion, and return on equity reached 13.8%.

Wells Fargo (NYSE:WFC) reports third-quarter 2026 results before the market opens on October 13. The bank provides loans, deposit accounts, and investment services. Its earnings per share, or profit divided by shares outstanding, reach $1.87, above the $1.85 analyst estimate.

The earnings beat comes even though revenue of $21.87 billion falls short of the $22.31 billion estimate. Revenue measures the money the bank brings in before expenses. As highlighted by Proactive Investors, earnings per share rise 13% from a year earlier, while net income increases 6% to $5.95 billion.

Wealth and Investment Management revenue grows 12% to $4.1 billion, as highlighted by Proactive Investors. Wells Fargo’s return on equity reaches 13.8%, above the 13.4% analysts expect. This measure shows how much profit the bank earns relative to shareholders’ investment.

Loan growth and interest income support the profit increase, as highlighted by Reuters. Interest income is money the bank earns from loans and other interest-paying assets. Wells Fargo has a trailing price-to-earnings ratio of 11.34, which compares its share price with earnings over the past 12 months.

items.title: Bank of America (NYSE: BAC) Q3 Earnings Preview: What to Watch
items.excerpt: Earnings Expectations: Wall Street anticipates earnings per share of $1.10 and revenue of $30.54 billion for the third quarter. Investment Banking & Trading Outlook: CEO Brian Moynihan projects a potential 10% decline in investment banking fees, with trading revenue expected to r
items.author: Danny Green
paragraphs: Earnings Expectations: Wall Street anticipates earnings per share of $1.10 and revenue of $30.54 billion for the third quarter.
Investment Banking & Trading Outlook: CEO Brian Moynihan projects a potential 10% decline in investment banking fees, with trading revenue expected to remain flat.
Stock Performance & Valuation: The stock has recently dropped 16% from its August peak, and it currently trades at a price-to-earnings ratio of 12.3 with a 2.35% dividend yield.

Bank of America (NYSE: BAC) is set to report its third-quarter earnings before the market opens on Wednesday, October 14, 2026. As the second-largest U.S. bank by assets, Bank of America generates significant revenue from consumer and business banking, lending, trading, and investment banking, competing with major financial institutions such as JPMorgan Chase (NYSE: JPM) and Wells Fargo (NYSE: WFC).

For the upcoming Q3 earnings report, Wall Street analysts expect earnings of $1.10 per share, an increase from $1.06 reported a year earlier. Analysts also anticipate revenue of $30.54 billion, up from $28.09 billion last year. These earnings per share (EPS) figures are crucial indicators of the bank's profitability for each share of its stock.

Investors will closely monitor the bank's trading and investment banking results. CEO Brian Moynihan has indicated that investment banking fees could see a 10% fall from the previous year, while trading revenue is expected to remain flat. Furthermore, higher bond yields could potentially raise the bank’s funding costs and make it more challenging for some borrowers to repay loans, impacting overall financial performance.

The BAC stock price has experienced a notable decline, falling from an August peak of $65.07 to $54.58, representing a drop of about 16%. This movement reflects broader pressure on U.S. bank stocks. Ahead of the earnings announcement, options trading suggests a possible move toward $57, as highlighted by Invezz. It's important to remember that options prices reflect market expectations, not a guaranteed stock price.

TD Cowen analyst R. Scott Siefers currently holds a Hold rating on Bank of America with a $60 price target. The bank offers a $0.32 quarterly dividend, which equates to $1.28 a year per share and a stated dividend yield of 2.35%. Its price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio is 12.3, indicating that shares are trading at 12.3 times the bank’s profit over the past year, a key valuation metric for investors.

items.author: Andrew Wynn
paragraphs: Insider Stock Sales: Sea Limited (NYSE:SE)'s Chief Compliance Officer, Wang Yanjun, has conducted multiple significant stock sales, reducing his holdings.
Recent Transaction Details: A recent sale on October 12, 2026, involved 312 shares for $29,739.84, following earlier transactions totaling over $300,000.00.
Key Financial Metrics: The company exhibits a trailing price-to-earnings ratio of 35.60 and a price-to-sales ratio of 2.09, indicating its current market valuation.

Sea Limited (NYSE:SE) operates digital entertainment, e-commerce and financial services businesses. Its Chief Compliance Officer and General Counsel, Wang Yanjun, sold 312 Class A ordinary shares on October 12, 2026, at $95.32 per share. The sale totaled $29,739.84 and left Wang with 82,468 shares.

The October 12 sale follows several earlier transactions. Wang sold 1,000 shares on October 2 at an average price of $95.15, receiving $95,150.00. That sale reduced Wang’s reported holdings by 1.13% to 87,780 shares, worth about $8.35 million at that price, as highlighted by Defense World.

Wang also sold 1,000 shares on September 30 at an average price of $97.67, for about $97,670.00. That transaction reduced reported holdings by 1.10% to 89,780 shares. Earlier sales included 1,000 shares on September 28 for $98,650.00 and 1,200 shares on September 25 for $120,048.00.

Sea Limited's trailing price-to-earnings ratio is 35.60, meaning its share price is 35.60 times its earnings per share over the past year. Its price-to-sales ratio is 2.09, while its enterprise value—which includes debt and subtracts cash—is 2.11 times trailing sales and 11.20 times trailing operating cash flow.

items.title: Goldman Sachs (NYSE: GS) Crushes Q3 Earnings Estimates with Strong Revenue Growth
items.excerpt: Goldman Sachs (NYSE: GS) reported impressive Q3 earnings and revenue , significantly surpassing analyst estimates. Growth was primarily fueled by a strong performance in Global Banking & Markets , particularly a 72% surge in equities revenue . The firm has consistently exceeded e
items.author: Danny Green
paragraphs: Goldman Sachs (NYSE: GS) reported impressive Q3 earnings and revenue, significantly surpassing analyst estimates.
Growth was primarily fueled by a strong performance in Global Banking & Markets, particularly a 72% surge in equities revenue.
The firm has consistently exceeded earnings-per-share estimates for the past four quarters, demonstrating robust financial momentum.

Goldman Sachs (NYSE: GS) reported stellar third-quarter earnings of $17.01 per share, significantly above the $12.86 estimate, and robust revenue of $18.68 billion, exceeding the $16.83 billion estimate. As a leading global investment bank, Goldman Sachs also manages substantial assets for clients. These impressive Q3 financial results were released before the market opened on October 13, 2026.

For the three months ended September 30, net revenue saw a substantial 23% rise from a year earlier, despite a slight dip from the previous quarter. Net earnings increased by an impressive 29% to $5.29 billion, with earnings per share climbing from $12.25 to $17.01, reflecting strong profitability.

Trading performance was a significant catalyst for much of this growth. Global Banking & Markets revenue climbed 32% to $13.46 billion, primarily driven by a remarkable 72% increase in equities revenue, reaching $6.44 billion. This strong equities trading figure comfortably beat expectations, although fixed-income and rates-trading revenue fell short of Wall Street estimates, as highlighted by Bloomberg Markets and Finance.

Furthermore, investment banking fees rose 21% to $3.22 billion, propelled by an increase in completed mergers and acquisitions and equity offerings. Asset & Wealth Management revenue also demonstrated solid growth, expanding 14% to $5.05 billion. As highlighted by Zacks, Goldman Sachs also surpassed its separate $12.90 earnings-per-share estimate, marking its fourth consecutive quarter of exceeding consensus earnings estimates.

An October 13 Stock Analysis snapshot lists Morgan Stanley’s trailing P/E at approximately 15.35 and its price-to-sales ratio at 3.80. That P/E implies an earnings yield of approximately 6.51%. These figures change with the share price and reported results; investors will also assess client flows, margins, and management’s outlook.

items.title: Truist Financial Boosts Price Target for Robinhood Markets (NASDAQ:HOOD) Amidst Investment Platform Competition
items.excerpt: Truist Financial has increased its price target for Robinhood Markets, signaling a more optimistic outlook for the investment platform. The updated price target of $134.00 suggests a potential 22% upside from recent trading levels. Robinhood Markets is also drawing attention from
items.author: Rayan Ahmad
paragraphs: Truist Financial has increased its price target for Robinhood Markets, signaling a more optimistic outlook for the investment platform.
The updated price target of $134.00 suggests a potential 22% upside from recent trading levels.
Robinhood Markets is also drawing attention from other analysts, with new coverage initiated by Evercore ISI Group.

Truist Financial, a prominent financial institution, has raised its price target for Robinhood Markets (NASDAQ:HOOD) to $134.00 from $130.00. Robinhood operates a popular app for trading stocks and other investments, positioning itself as a key player in the digital investment platform space and competing with established brokerage firms such as Charles Schwab and Fidelity. A price target represents an analyst’s estimate of where a stock could trade, reflecting their market outlook.

Robinhood stock was trading at $109.87 when Truist's updated stock analysis was published. The new $134.00 target is $24.13 higher, implying approximately 22% upside potential from that price. While raising a price target signals a higher estimate of the stock’s value and a positive market outlook, it does not guarantee that the stock will reach that specific level.

items.author: Alex Lavoie
paragraphs: UBS and Truist Securities maintain cautious ratings (Neutral/Hold) on IBM, reflecting uncertainty in its near-term growth.
Analysts question the timing of increased corporate spending on AI infrastructure and its impact on demand for IBM's products and services.
Despite potential in key offerings like Red Hat and watsonx Orchestrate, concerns about execution and customer demand timing persist.

IBM (NYSE: IBM) provides essential business software, mainframes, and consulting services. Its innovative offerings include Red Hat software and watsonx Orchestrate, which are crucial for helping companies manage complex AI-related work. UBS, a prominent financial institution, reiterates its Neutral rating on IBM, suggesting a recommendation to hold rather than buy or sell the stock. IBM traded at $232.47 when UBS published this rating on October 13, 2026.

Truist Securities also adopts a cautious perspective on the tech giant. It initiates coverage with a Hold rating and sets a price target of $240.00, reflecting an analyst’s estimate of where the stock could trade. Truist raises critical questions regarding the timeline for increased corporate spending on AI infrastructure to translate into stronger demand for IBM’s diverse products and services.

Analyst Arvind Ramnani identifies significant potential within IBM’s core offerings, including its robust mainframes, innovative watsonx Orchestrate platform, leading Red Hat software, and extensive consulting business. However, the precise timing of increased customer demand remains uncertain. Truist also expresses concerns about IBM’s ability to effectively execute its strategic plans, a point further emphasized by GuruFocus.

In a recent market snapshot, IBM shares traded at $231.64, marking an increase of $4.62, or 2.04%. During the trading day, shares fluctuated between $227.28 and $233.50, while the 52-week range spanned from $199.19 to $332.46. IBM’s current market value stands at approximately $218.24 billion, with 1.15 million shares traded.

items.author: Gordon Thompson
paragraphs: UnitedHealth Group (NYSE: UNH) exceeded adjusted earnings per share estimates for Q3 2026, reporting $4.69 per share.
The healthcare giant also surpassed revenue expectations, reaching $112.70 billion, demonstrating robust financial performance.
UnitedHealth Group raised its full-year outlook, reflecting strong operational momentum, which led to its shares rising 4% to $395.19 after the report.

UnitedHealth Group (NYSE: UNH) provides health insurance and health care services. It competes with insurers such as Humana. In the third quarter of 2026, UnitedHealth Group reports adjusted earnings of $4.69 per share, above the $4.14 estimate in the initial figures. Earnings per share show how much profit the company reports for each share.

Revenue reaches $112.70 billion, above the $111.30 billion estimate. More detailed results put revenue at $112.69 billion, slightly below $113.16 billion a year earlier. Adjusted earnings rise from $2.92 per share a year earlier to $4.69.

As highlighted by Zacks, the $4.69 earnings figure also exceeds its separate $4.12 consensus estimate. UnitedHealth Group beats consensus earnings estimates in each of the past four quarters and revenue estimates in three. Its medical-cost ratio is 88.4%, meaning medical care costs account for 88.4 cents of each premium dollar. UnitedHealth Group raises its full-year outlook again, as highlighted by MarketWatch.

Shares rise 4% to $395.19 after the report, as highlighted by 24/7 Wall St. UnitedHealth Group’s trailing price-to-earnings ratio is 24.16, meaning its share price is 24.16 times its earnings over the past year. Its price-to-sales ratio is 0.76, comparing the company’s market value with its annual revenue.

items.author: Andrew Wynn
paragraphs: Analysts anticipate BlackRock (NYSE: BLK) to report $14.32 earnings per share on $7.43 billion in revenue for Q3 2026, representing a 21.6% rise in EPS and 14.5% revenue growth year-over-year.
The investment management giant has a strong track record, consistently beating adjusted earnings estimates in the past four quarters.

Despite strong past performance, the company faces potential challenges from rising expenses and lower performance fees, with its trailing price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio at 25.32 and price-to-sales (P/S) ratio at 6.09.

BlackRock (NYSE: BLK) reports third-quarter 2026 earnings before the market opens on Wednesday, October 14. The company manages investments for clients and competes with firms such as State Street (NYSE: STT), which also reports that day. Wall Street expects BlackRock to earn $14.32 per share on revenue of approximately $7.43 billion.

As highlighted by Zacks Investment Research, analysts expect BlackRock’s earnings per share to rise 21.6% from a year earlier, with revenue up 14.5%. Assets under management—the value of investments BlackRock oversees for clients—are expected to grow 16.4%, helped by rising markets and money flowing into its funds.

BlackRock beats adjusted earnings estimates in each of the past four quarters, as highlighted by Zacks Investment Research. In the most recent quarter, it earns $13.91 per share against an estimate of $12.67. The quarter before that, it earns $12.53 per share against an estimate of $11.46.

Those past results set a high bar for the October report. Jim Cramer says BlackRock, Morgan Stanley (NYSE: MS) and State Street are “priced for disappointment,” meaning their share prices may leave little room for weaker-than-expected results. Rising expenses and lower performance fees—payments tied to investment results—could also weigh on BlackRock’s earnings.

BlackRock’s trailing price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio is 25.32, meaning its shares trade at 25.32 times its earnings over the past year. Its price-to-sales ratio is 6.09, meaning investors pay $6.09 for each $1 of annual revenue. These figures give investors a way to judge the share price alongside the upcoming results.
